title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with datasets exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based approaches incur quadratic complexity. The paper proposes SVEAD, which constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchor points and scores each point by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale (δmean). Experiments on 45 ADBench datasets show SVEAD achieves state-of-the-art average AUC-ROC and AUC-PR with linear time complexity, outperforming 12 baselines.

match_target.why: The user explicitly hinted at Table 4, SVEAD AUC-ROC on cardio. This is a concrete per-dataset result that directly exercises the core scoring mechanism (dual-factor Voronoi cell scoring with ensemble averaging) on a real benchmark, and the paper reports both the mean and standard deviation needed for a tight tolerance band.

tolerance.why: Rule 1 applies: the paper reports a standard deviation over 5 repeated runs for the target value (Table 5, cardio, VEAD = 0.0063). The absolute band is 3 x 0.0063 = 0.0189, already at the 4-decimal precision the paper prints.

requirements.stmt: For each partition, sample m anchor points uniformly from the dataset without replacement.
requirements.quote: we randomly sample m points from the dataset X without replacement to form an anchor set

requirements.stmt: Assign every data point to its nearest anchor using Euclidean distance, forming Voronoi cells.
requirements.quote: Each point x ∈X is assigned to its nearest anchor

requirements.stmt: For each cell, compute the maximum distance δmax and mean distance δmean from the anchor to all points in the cell.
Score each point using the dual-factor formula s(x) = (δ/δmax) · δmean.
If a cell contains only the anchor (|Ci| = 1), skip scoring for that point in that partition.
requirements.quote: we skip scoring for this point in this partition

requirements.stmt: Aggregate scores across all t partitions by arithmetic mean to produce the final anomaly score.
requirements.quote: The final anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean

requirements.stmt: Use ensemble size t = 100 and search the number of anchors m over {21, 22, ..., 28}.
requirements.quote: the number of sample points is searched over {21, 22, . . . , 28}, with ensemble size fixed at 100

requirements.stmt: Repeat the full experiment 5 times and report the average performance.
requirements.quote: we repeat experiments 5 times and report the average performance

requirements.stmt: Evaluate using AUC-ROC and AUC-PR, with labels used only after predictions are made.
requirements.quote: We adopt Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and Area Under the Precision-Recall curve (AUC-PR)

requirements.stmt: Operate in the unsupervised setting where the detector scores all points without access to labels.
